evidence.fit_with_native_workflow: Instructor is not an agent SDK/runtime in the sense the incumbent list uses the term (Claude Code, Codex, claude-agent-sdk-python, LangGraph, agent-framework, etc.); it is a typed structured-output extraction wrapper. It does not fit as a workflow-harness layer (no dispatch, no sessions, no worker/isolation model of its own — C2 and C3 are effectively inherited/not applicable rather than satisfied). Its only credible fit in this project is as a narrowly-scoped Pydantic-model extraction utility that a deterministic pipeline step could call directly against an already-authenticated provider client (e.g., inside an isolated-builder or evidence-reviewer step that needs typed parsing of an LLM response) — not as a replacement for the Claude Code/Codex native workers, Workflow tool, or the typesafe-ai skill's judgment contract. The project's own AGENTS.md 'C1 native-auth fit' criterion is a real penalty here: it requires a separate paid provider API key/env var per provider rather than riding a Claude Code, Codex, GitHub, or Google native login, and it adds nothing on the sandbox/isolation axis (C3) since it has no execution environment of its own — deterministic code retains ownership either way.
evidence.interface: Pure Python SDK/library (`pip install instructor`), no CLI, server or daemon. Usage pattern: `client = instructor.from_provider("openai/gpt-4o")` wraps/patches an existing provider client object, then `client.chat.completions.create(response_model=PydanticModel, messages=[...])` returns a validated, typed Pydantic object instead of raw JSON. Supports streaming of `Partial[Model]` objects, nested Pydantic models, and automatic validation-retry loops on `field_validator` failures. Multi-language variants exist (Python is the reviewed one; also TypeScript, Go, Ruby per docs site) but this review covers the Python package only, matching the repo audited.
evidence.isolation_model: No isolation/sandbox model of its own. It runs in-process with the caller, invoking whatever HTTP client/session the wrapped provider SDK already uses; there is no worktree, sandbox, or process boundary concept in the library. Per-call state is just the Pydantic response model and retry loop; there is no hidden global state beyond normal Python module import, so multiple callers can each hold independent wrapped clients without cross-talk (deterministic code fully owns the effects, satisfying C3 only in the trivial sense that there is nothing to isolate).

evidence.summary: 567-labs/instructor is an MIT-licensed, actively maintained (v1.17.0, 2026-09-09; last push 2026-09-18; 13,935 stars) pure-Python SDK that patches a caller-supplied LLM provider client (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Ollama, etc.) so `create()` calls return validated Pydantic objects instead of raw JSON, with automatic validation-retry and partial-object streaming. It has upstream tests/ and multiple CI workflows (test.yml, ty.yml, ruff.yml, evals.yml, mutation.yml, scheduled-release.yml). It is a library, not a server or agent runtime: no isolation/sandbox model, no structured events/resumable sessions, and no MCP/tool dispatch were found in its docs. Authentication is entirely caller-supplied (provider API keys via env vars or an explicit `api_key` argument) — there is no native Claude Code/Codex/GitHub/Google login path, matching the judges' recorded C1 penalty. The README itself frames Instructor as a narrower sibling of pydantic-ai ("Use Instructor for fast extraction, reach for PydanticAI when you need agents"), supporting the judges' targeted_candidate / keep_but_compare framing: it is worth a bounded, executed comparison (instructor-typed extraction vs the typesafe-ai skill and vs pydantic-ai on a shared extraction fixture) rather than adoption, since agreement among the three judges' shortlist reasons does not itself promote it per the project's evidence policy.

evidence.worker_features: No worker/dispatch model. Instructor has no concept of spawning workers, agents, or parallel tasks; it is a single synchronous or async call wrapper (`client.chat.completions.create(...)`, with an `async_client=True` option per `from_provider`) that returns one validated object per call. Retry behavior (`max_retries=N`) re-issues the same underlying provider call with the validation error appended, which is the closest analogue to a "worker" retry loop, but there is no multi-worker orchestration, custom tool registry, or MCP integration documented.

evidence.summary: anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-typescript (@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk) is Anthropic's official Node/TS headless-agent library that runs the Claude Code binary as a subprocess, exposing query(), session resume/fork, custom SDK-MCP tools, subagents and structured message streaming. Its official docs and quickstart explicitly require ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (or Bedrock/Vertex/AWS/Foundry credentials) and state Anthropic does not allow third-party products to offer claude.ai/Claude Code login, which refutes all three shortlisted judges' C1 fit claims that this repo clears the user's existing Claude Code subscription login. The repo has no license grant (LICENSE.md is 'All rights reserved' under Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service, matching the GitHub API's null/NOASSERTION field), no tests directory, and its .github/workflows are repo-maintenance automation (issue triage, non-write-user gating, Slack notification), not a build/test CI pipeline, so 'has_ci=true' in the source data overstates what CI actually verifies.
evidence.interface: npm package @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk (Node.js 18+). Primary entry point query({prompt, options}) returns an AsyncGenerator<SDKMessage> streaming Claude's reasoning, tool calls, tool results and a final ResultMessage; accepts a string prompt or an AsyncIterable<SDKUserMessage> for multi-turn/streaming input. Session helpers: startup() (pre-warm CLI subprocess), listSessions(), getSessionMessages(), getSessionInfo(), renameSession(), tagSession(); resume option continues the most recent session, forkSession creates a new session id from an existing transcript. Bundles native Claude Code platform binaries (darwin-arm64, linux-x64 glibc/musl, win32-x64) as npm optional dependencies, or falls back to pathToClaudeCodeExecutable for a natively installed Claude Code CLI. A non-JS caller can instead run the CLI as a subprocess with `-p --output-format json` per docs.
evidence.auth_model: Docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/quickstart) require setting ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the Claude Console as an environment variable read by the process (the SDK does not load .env files itself), with alternate first-party-cloud paths: Amazon Bedrock (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1 + AWS credentials), Claude Platform on AWS (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS=1 + ANTHROPIC_AWS_WORKSPACE_ID), Google Cloud's Agent Platform (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1 + GCP credentials), and Microsoft Foundry (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY=1 + Azure credentials). Quoted directly from the docs: "Unless previously approved, Anthropic does not allow third party developers to offer claude.ai login or rate limits for their products, including agents built on the Claude Agent SDK. Use the API key authentication methods described in the Quickstart instead." This appears twice (overview page and quickstart page) and is an explicit policy statement, not an implementation gap.
evidence.isolation_model: Runs as a local subprocess (the bundled or externally installed Claude Code binary) under the caller's OS process, not a managed sandbox by default. permissionMode governs tool execution: 'default' (prompts), 'plan' (read-only + planModeInstructions), 'bypassPermissions' (requires allowDangerouslySkipPermissions: true), plus project/local-settings-only 'auto'. Fine-grained control via allowedTools/disallowedTools (scoped rules like "Bash(rm *)"), additionalDirectories, and a canUseTool callback for custom permission logic invoked only when the built-in flow would otherwise prompt. cwd sets the working directory (default process.cwd()); projectConfigRoot can point Claude Code's settings/.mcp.json/commands/agents/skills resolution at a separate trusted checkout from cwd. resolveSettings() and managedSettings support MDM/policy-tier configuration merged as restrictive-only. No SDK-level container/VM sandbox is described in the fetched docs; isolation is whatever the host process/OS provides.
evidence.worker_features: tool() builds type-safe in-process MCP tool definitions from Zod 3/4 schemas with ToolAnnotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint); createSdkMcpServer() packages tools into an in-process MCP server (with alwaysLoad/timeout/instructions). External MCP servers are configured via mcpServers: Record<string, McpServerConfig>, with onElicitation for MCP elicitation callbacks and deferred tool loading via searchHint. Subagents: the `agent` option names the main-thread agent persona; `agents` programmatically defines subagent Record<string, AgentDefinition>; agentProgressSummaries and forwardSubagentText control how subagent activity (task_progress events, nested text/thinking) surfaces to the parent stream with parent_tool_use_id/parent_agent_id lineage tags. Hooks, skills, commands, memory and plugins load from .claude/ and ~/.claude/ the same as the Claude Code CLI per the SDK overview capabilities table.
evidence.structured_events: SDKMessage is a union covering SDKUserMessage (streaming input), SDKTaskProgressMessage (with optional summary), SDKHookStartedMessage/SDKHookProgressMessage/SDKHookResponseMessage (gated by includeHookEvents), partial/delta messages (includePartialMessages), and a prompt_suggestion message (promptSuggestions option). Assistant/tool/result messages carry a `type` discriminator (e.g. 'assistant', 'result') and content blocks; nested/subagent messages carry parent_tool_use_id and parent_agent_id for lineage. This matches C2 (structured events, resumable sessions, custom tools/MCP).
evidence.tests_and_ci: No `tests` directory in the top-level tree (gh api repos/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-typescript/contents lists only .claude, .github, CHANGELOG.md, LICENSE.md, README.md, examples, scripts) — confirms has_tests_dir=false from the source data. .github/workflows contains issue-triage.yml, non-write-users-check.yml, and slack-issue-notification.yml only: these are repository-maintenance/community-ops automations, not a build/lint/test pipeline. No evidence of any unit/integration test suite or CI check that runs code against the package; upstream tests could not be located in this packet.
evidence.license: GitHub API license field is null (NOASSERTION), consistent with the shortlist's flagged gate. LICENSE.md itself is not a template license: full text is "© Anthropic PBC. All rights reserved. Use is subject to Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service." — i.e. the repository is explicitly proprietary/all-rights-reserved under a commercial ToS, not merely missing a license declaration. README and docs confirm: "Use of the Claude Agent SDK is governed by Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service... except to the extent a specific component or dependency is covered by a different license as indicated in that component's LICENSE file." This is stronger than NOASSERTION alone and should be recorded as 'proprietary/commercial ToS', not merely 'license missing'.
evidence.maintenance: Very active: releases roughly daily-to-every-few-days (v0.3.274 to v0.3.278 across 2026-09-17 to 2026-09-19 alone); repo created 2025-09-27, last pushed 2026-09-19T03:10:32Z, last updated 2026-09-22T15:35:25Z; 1,762 stargazers, 228 forks, 216 open issues; Discord community channel and GitHub issue tracker referenced in README. evidence.portability: Bundles native binaries via npm optional dependencies for macOS arm64 (Apple Silicon), Linux x64 glibc and musl, and Windows x64; falls back to pathToClaudeCodeExecutable pointing at a natively installed Claude Code CLI when optional deps are skipped (e.g. npm ci --omit=optional) or unsupported (e.g. some ARM64 Windows/pip cases documented for the Python sibling). This covers the required Linux/WSL2 x86_64 and macOS arm64 targets (C6) directly via the linux-x64 and darwin-arm64 optional packages.

However, the auth-model finding is decisive: the SDK cannot run on the user's existing Claude Code subscription login for a third-party integration per Anthropic's own documented policy, so any local_integration acceptance run (e.g. the shortlisted `rtk proxy node tests/integration/claude-agent-sdk-ts-smoke.mjs` with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset) would be expected to fail authentication or fall back to no credentials at all, not resolve to a Claude Code login source as the gap-first judge's acceptance command implicitly assumed.

The only differentiator this packet can confirm is language (Node/TS vs Python) for out-of-Claude-Code programmatic embedding — a real but narrow capability gap (C5), not the 'Claude Code login it uses natively' capability the judges claimed.

Runs as a local subprocess with no described sandbox beyond permission modes/tool allow-deny lists; C3 isolation depends entirely on the caller's own process/OS controls (e.g. this project's worktree/sandbox conventions), not anything the SDK itself enforces.

The shortlisted local_integration acceptance command (`rtk proxy node tests/integration/claude-agent-sdk-ts-smoke.mjs` with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset asserting a resolved 'Claude Code login' auth source) is built on the now-refuted auth assumption and should be revised or dropped before being run as written.
